lots.findings: Moorcroft Leaf and Berry (Autumn leaf) pattern on cobalt blue ground, squat ovoid vase. Base impressed 'MADE IN ENGLAND' and blue painted W. Moorcroft signature with 'POTTER TO H.M. THE QUEEN' paper label/stamp, placing it in Walter Moorcroft era c.1950s-70s.
lots.condition: No visible chips or cracks; base clean.
lots.identification: Moorcroft Leaf and Berry (autumn leaves with blackberries) small globular/ovoid vase on a deep cobalt blue ground, short neck and foot, about 11 cm. lots.findings: American acorn form shelf clock with bentwood laminated case, side arms with acorn finials, painted floral dial, reverse-painted/etched glass tablet. lots.identification: American 'acorn' shelf clock, J.C. Brown / Forestville Manufacturing Co, Bristol (Forestville) Connecticut, c.1847-50. Laminated (bent-ply) rosewood/mahogany-look acorn-form case with laminated side arms and turned acorn finials on a stepped base, 65 cm high. Pointed upper door glass over a painted zinc dial (Roman numerals, pink-rose and gilt-leaf spandrels, no maker name visible on the dial in the photo), lower door with frosted/etched glass tablet in a feather-and-cross pattern with small coloured roundels. Inside: brass bell, brass-covered pendulum bob, and a torn printed paper label 'CLOCK MANUFACTORY / J. C. BROWN' with a woodcut vignette and text columns, the backboard paper mostly torn away. A brass fitting at the base, which could be the top of the detached fusees or a winding key. Looks period, not a modern copy, but this can't be confirmed from three 450x600 photos.

lots.title: OLD LEATHER BOUND LEDGER USED ...
lots.findings: Full leather gilt-tooled ledger used as a 19th-century commonplace book: alphabet index tabs, handwritten recipes (Gooseberry Fool), parlour games, 'Gun Powder' trial notes dated Sept 1869 or 1884 (Curtis and Harvey's? diamond grain trials), plus loose letters, a pencil sketch of figures in landscape, printed circulars and an envelope with stamps. Provenance and place unknown; could be Tasmanian.
lots.condition: Leather rubbed and scuffed, spine worn, contents loose.
lots.identification: Late Victorian full-calf gilt-ruled ledger/album (blind and gilt fillet panels, corner fleurons, raised-band spine with fleurons, no title) with an alphabet thumb index (coloured A-Z tabs), used as a family commonplace book: neat manuscript entries including 'Gooseberry Fool' recipe, a list of parlour 'Games' (Blind Man's Buff, Twenty Questions, Geography etc.), and a 'Gun Powder' trial note dated Sept 1884 comparing Curtis & Harvey's Diamond Grain black powder with a 'White Powder' (penetration of 56 pages of a book by 7 shots), plus 'Gallo Gal...' recipe. Loose with it: a handwritten letter on blue squared paper, a pencil sketch of figures with a horse/animals in a landscape (unsigned as far as visible), a blue printed legal-looking form beginning 'Her Majesty' / 'Greeting' (writ or commission, Victorian era) and blue manuscript sheets with an envelope bearing a single red stamp and circular postmarks. Origin (English or colonial) not determinable from the photos.

No ..'), parties incl. John Kemp(?) and a widow; it is an abstract (later copy), not an original 1841 deed. (2) A folded Mortgage with the Tasmanian Permanent Executors and Trustees Association, dated 19x9 (looks 1919 or 1929). (3) 'Subdivision Sale Westwood Estate' booklet, for the Tasmanian Woolgrowers Agency Company Limited, Launceston. (4) 'Handbook of Tasmanian Emergency Legislation' (WWII-era, government printer). (5) Blue booklet 'Directions for the erection of domestic surface shelters' (WWII air-raid shelters). (6) Tasmanian Football Record, 1960s (Heathorns Morris 1100 advert on cover). (7) Greyhound racing programme (Tasmanian club, 1960s). (8) 1917 cover 'Tasmania' postmark 14 SEP 17 addressed to Woodlands(?), Ringarooma, Tasmania, KGV red stamp; another cover/card. (9) Real-photo prints: a locomotive in a tunnel/shed, an oval landscape photo, newspaper cuttings ('Orange Blossom' wedding). (10) Small bag of loose stamps (common KGV reds etc) and a student ticket. (11) Two railway dog spikes tied with a handwritten tag 'Clyde dog spikes type used at Tasmania mining sites on light rail lines'. (12) A small cast zinc slab stamped 'Electrolytic Zinc Australasia' with lightning-bolt logo, three panels (EZ Co, Risdon souvenir ingot/sample, with a brass peg).

lots.identification: Omega mechanical stopwatch, black crackle/textured finish case with crown-pusher and two side pushers, steel bow. Back painted in green with NATO stock number 6645-66-031-3804 (6645 = time measuring instruments, 66 = Australia): Australian Defence issue, likely 1970s. Same family as the Australian-issue 'Omega stop watch 6645 PN MG 6301 PW73/..' examples sold on eBay AU in 2024. Lot page: estimate A$120-180; bid dropdown starts at A$75, so current bid about A$70.
